evidence: task/task.toml [environment] (lines 20-24) contains only build_timeout_sec = 600.0, network_mode = "public", cpus = 2, memory_mb = 4096; no docker_image key. Recursive grep for 'docker_image' and 'image *=' across the whole frozen task tree and the frozen template returned no matches, so [verifier.environment] (lines 37-38) has none either. The agent Dockerfile task/environment/Dockerfile has active build steps (FROM node:22-bookworm-slim, apt-get install, npm install -g express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1, COPY instructions/ and assets/, git-init of /app), and with no docker_image these steps are what actually build the agent image; nothing shadows them. task.toml is byte-identical in hash (ac664d0e...) between the frozen snapshot and projects/hireops-recruiting-operations/hireops-recruiting-operations/task.toml, and environment/Dockerfile likewise (0a75419e...), so the working copy has not drifted on this row. Both Dockerfiles diff-identical to the frozen template's, and task.toml [environment]/[verifier] sections match the template exactly, so no template-controlled setting was altered. Counterfactual: if someone set [environment].docker_image to a prebuilt image, the instructions/assets COPY and /app git-init would be silently skipped and a model could see a world differing from the brief; this task does not do that. A conforming alternative cannot fail this row because it concerns only task wiring, not the submission. Colderwater lessons (brief voice, weights, judge timing, modifier clicks, public URLs, restart checks, double grading, prompt size) do not bear on this wiring row; no instance found. This is a static source check; no Docker build was run by this reviewer (none needed to establish absence of the key).
